lanes.summary: The change is mostly sound: `reasoning_options` correctly maps `"off"`/`""` to disabled reasoning and passes other efforts through, the wire from config to gateway is tested, and the pricing tests cover the new models and argument-order hazards. One concern: the new `reasoning_effort` field on `Models` has no visible `#[serde(default)]`, so config files that omit it may fail to deserialize — but this depends on whether the struct has a container-level default that I cannot see from the diff.

The PR adds a configurable reasoning effort setting for the OpenRouter gateway, switches default models to cheaper alternatives, and updates the pricing table accordingly. Tests cover the new `reasoning_options` function, verify the setting reaches the gateway, assert all default-selected models have prices, and pin cost figures including argument ordering for `completion_cost`. Nothing sensitive found in what this pull request commits.

The PR title and body accurately describe the diff: the scan/deep models are moved from minimax-m3 and kimi-k3 to z-ai/glm-5.2, the fallback chain is changed to deepseek-v4-pro and minimax-m3, reasoning becomes configurable via a new `reasoning_effort` field (defaulting to `"high"`) instead of being hard-disabled, and every model named in the description gets a price entry in `harness::pricing`. The description's claims about the fallback chain, reasoning hazard, tier separation, and verification (fmt/clippy/test counts) all correspond to concrete code and test additions in the diff. No significant change in the diff is left unmentioned, and nothing in the description claims a change the diff does not make.
